why: The tip blade slides 0.3-5 cm behind the teeth and can seal the full bore. That gives a /t/ seal at 0.3-1.5 cm. It can also form an /s/ channel near the ridge, where a front cavity of about 1.5-2 cm gives 4.4-5.8 kHz, and an /ʃ/ channel at 2-3 cm, where a front cavity of about 3-4 cm gives 2.2-2.9 kHz. For /tɑ/ the body pad can hold the /ɑ/ posture (place about 9.5) while the tip seals and releases, so the rail servo does not need its 78-degree turn. A body stroke of 1.3 cm pushes the pad past the 1.2 cm bore radius, sealing the velar place for /k/. Two constrictions at once may also lower F3 for /ɝ/. No cam_tongue value reaches the front of the mouth, because rail_start is at least 2.5 cm. Cost: $12 (pushrod kit plus 1 servo), 3 days, 76 machine minutes.

Round_lips closes from 0 cm2 (a seal for /p/ with the tongue and airway open) and protrudes the lip tube up to 1.6 cm past the teeth (tract 14.5 cm up to about 16.1 cm). Rounding plus a back tongue constriction should bring F2 down to about 850-1000 Hz while F1 stays at 300-570 Hz. The jaw_lips range of values cannot do this: its rest_area is at least 2.5 cm2 and it has no protrusion, so no params move helps. Cost: $4 pushrod kit, 2 days, 57 machine minutes. Servos: the jaw servo is reused and the one on hand is used.
